leftEvidence.title: Israel is called firstborn and Pharaoh is warned about his firstborn son

points.label: Firstborn identities
points.left: Israel and Pharaoh’s son are placed in a direct warning.
points.right: Egyptian firstborn across social positions and livestock are struck.

points.label: Demand and response
points.left: Release for service is demanded before Pharaoh’s refusal.
points.right: Pharaoh summons Moses and orders Israel to depart and serve.

points.label: Scope
points.left: The warning is compressed into two verses.
points.right: The night expands through death, crying, urgency, dough, and received goods.

payload.posture: Keep each Scripture witness intact, inspect what each states, and do not supply a combined sequence the sources do not author.

rightEvidence.title: Egypt’s firstborn die from throne to dungeon before Israel is released

payload.tension: The earlier saying frames the conflict through firstborn sonship before the later account narrates the night’s wider reach.
payload.title: Firstborn warning and firstborn night
